task.title: Issue #20 exact CONNECTION_CLOSE packet replay
task.summary: Five attempts resolved 2 validation failures and 2 blocked reviews before approval and integration.

causes.detail: The completed plan released the first worker attempt.
Cached close replays bypass outbound observability
Opt-in exact replay skips application-initiated closes
Review approved the attempt for integration.

plan.objective: Implement issue #20 as a default-off transport mode that caches the first successfully protected CONNECTION_CLOSE datagram and replays its exact bytes for eligible closing-state responses, while retaining existing rate limiting and anti-amplification enforcement.
plan.sourceContext: GitHub issue #20 · connection: replay exact close packet while closing
constraints: Do not implement or fetch any issue other than #20.
Do not alter GitHub issue state, labels, comments, commits, branches, or remotes.
Do not add general-purpose protected-packet replay or change ordinary QUIC retransmission behavior.
Do not redesign peer CONNECTION_CLOSE handling, key-retention behavior, or closing/draining deadlines.
Do not expand language bindings or the C FFI unless later issue text explicitly requires it.

steps.detail: At implementation start, query only issue #20 with `gh issue view 20 -R minhuw/coquic` and stop if it is no longer open or its full acceptance criteria conflict with this plan. Do not list or fetch other issues.
steps.title: Confirm selected issue

steps.detail: Add the default-off `replay_exact_close_packet_while_closing` transport setting to the public C++ configuration, map it into the internal QUIC transport configuration, and cover construction through the public API.
steps.title: Plumb opt-in configuration

steps.detail: Add connection-owned storage for the first successfully emitted serialized close image. Retain it only while the connection is in closing mode, and clear it on draining transition and closing-period expiry so stale protected bytes cannot escape their closing lifecycle.
steps.title: Model cached close state

steps.detail: In the closing send path, preserve current close packet construction and commit behavior for the first send, then cache its exact protected bytes when the option is enabled. For later rate-limited responses, return a copy of the cache without reserving packet numbers, serializing, protecting, incrementing encryption counters, or adding duplicate recovery records. Apply the current outbound size and amplification checks before replay, and on success update outbound byte accounting, response-threshold state, selected path, and ECN metadata exactly once.
steps.title: Replay exact protected image

steps.detail: Extend the focused closing lifecycle tests to prove enabled replays are byte-identical, decode to the same packet number and key phase, and leave the next packet number and AEAD-encryption count unchanged. Add a default-off control proving current regeneration remains distinct. Exercise the existing 2, 4, and subsequent response thresholds with cached replay, and verify an unvalidated server path blocks a replay that exceeds its remaining three-times budget, preserves pending state and counters while blocked, then emits the identical image and charges its full size after sufficient inbound credit.
steps.title: Add focused replay tests

steps.detail: Review the focused diff for unintended API or closing-state changes, then run the repository build and complete test suite in the reproducible development environment.
steps.title: Validate focused patch

reviews.summary: Block: the feature's wire behavior is focused and the required build and test suite pass, but cached retransmissions bypass existing outbound telemetry.

findings.detail: Cached replay returns after only byte accounting, bypassing the normal commit path. Replayed packets therefore emit no `quic:packet_sent` qlog event, queue no outbound packet-inspection effect, and do not update send-profile datagram counters. This makes actual wire sends invisible whenever those existing observability features are enabled.
findings.recommendation: Add replay-specific send bookkeeping that preserves exact bytes and avoids re-encryption/retracking, while emitting qlog, packet-inspection, and profile updates. Cache the metadata/snapshot needed for that bookkeeping and add a focused replay observability test.
findings.title: Cached close replays bypass outbound observability

validationGaps: `nix develop -c zig build` and `nix develop -c zig build test` passed.
The QUIC RAG backend could not be queried because its configured backend was unavailable and the local Qdrant REST port was already occupied.
reviews.remainingRisk: Rate limiting, packet-number/protection reuse, default behavior, and amplification accounting are covered by the added tests.

reviews.summary: Block: transport-close replay is implemented and the required build/test commands pass, but the opt-in does not replay the initial public application-close packet exactly.

findings.detail: A locally initiated application close takes the normal application send path, enters closing at line 5338, and commits at this line. The cache is populated only by the pre-existing closing-path send at line 1820. Consequently, with the opt-in enabled, a later close response finds no cache and reserializes the APPLICATION_CLOSE with a new packet number and protection, rather than replaying its original bytes. This affects the public close-connection path.
findings.recommendation: Populate the exact-close cache after a successful locally initiated application-close commit as well, preferably through shared close-send caching logic. Add a focused `queue_application_close` test asserting identical replay bytes and unchanged packet/protection state.
findings.title: Opt-in exact replay skips application-initiated closes

reviews.remainingRisk: The local Qdrant RAG backend could not start (exit code 1), so protocol review relied on the repository's existing RFC 9000 §10.2.1 enforcement and tests.

reviews.summary: Approved. The focused nine-file patch adds an opt-in public configuration, caches the protected close datagram, replays identical bytes without advancing packet-number/protection state, retains exponential close-response limiting, and applies existing per-path amplification accounting. Build and all 1,762 tests passed.
validationGaps: Independent QUIC RAG lookup was unavailable in this worktree; the local Qdrant service could not start because its port was in use.
reviews.remainingRisk: No material code risk identified. The configured QUIC RAG backend could not be queried because port 6333 was already occupied and the index was unavailable.
